stem: By passing, 'Triple Talaq law' recently, the Parliament of India endorsed which year's ruling of the Supreme Court of India that had made Triple Talaq (Talaq-e-Biddat) as unconstitutional?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In Shayara Bano v. Union of India and Others, a five-judge bench of the Supreme Court, in a landmark judgment in 2017, held the practice of triple talaq (talaq-e-biddat) unconstitutional, declaring it a violation of Article 14 of the Constitution. In support of this judgment, the Parliament of India enacted the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019, making the practice of triple talaq (instant talaq on the basis of pronouncing talaq three times, including in written and electronic form) legally invalid and unlawful.

stem: With reference to the Consumer Disputes Redressal at the district level in India, which one of the following statements is not correct?

options.label: a
options.text: The District Forum entertains the complaints where the value of goods or services does not exceed rupees fifty lakhs.

options.label: b
options.text: The State Government can establish more than one District Forum in a district if it deems fit.

options.label: c
options.text: One of the members of the District Forum shall be a woman.

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 provides a three-tier quasi-judicial mechanism for the resolution of consumer disputes, which includes the District Commission, State Commission, and National Commission. Under this Act, the State Government shall establish a District Commission and, if it deems fit, may establish more than one District Commission in a district. The District Commission consists of a President (qualified to be a District Judge) and at least two members; at least one among the President or the members must be a woman (and the minimum age for both the President and members is 35 years). The jurisdiction of the District Commissions includes complaints where the value paid for goods or services does not exceed `50 lakh.

options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: India’s Supreme Court is a federal court. It is also the protector of human rights and the final interpreter of the Constitution; therefore, option (e) is the correct answer.

stem: Supreme Court in India was established-

options.label: a
options.text: By an Act of Parliament in 1950

expl: The Supreme Court of India is the highest judicial body under the Constitution of India. Article 124 of the Constitution states that “There shall be a Supreme Court of India.” With the commencement of the Constitution on 26 January 1950, the Supreme Court came into existence. Before shifting in 1958 to its present building on Tilak Marg, New Delhi, it functioned in the Old Parliament House. On 28 January 1950, two days after India became a fully sovereign democratic republic, the Supreme Court was inaugurated. It was inaugurated in the Chamber of Princes in the Old Parliament House, where the Federal Court of India had functioned for 12 years (from 1937 to 1950).

stem: Which one of the following statements is not correct?

options.label: a
options.text: The Supreme Court was established in 1950.

options.label: b
options.text: The Supreme Court is the highest court in the country where appeals are made.

options.label: c
options.text: The Supreme Court can hear any High Court/Courts except Court-Martial.

options.label: d
options.text: The Supreme Court can hear any High Court/Courts along with Court-Martial.

expl: Under the provisions of the Armed Forces Tribunal Act, 2007, appeals against court-martial decisions can ultimately be made to the Supreme Court as well.

stem: Currently, the number of Supreme Court judges is-

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More then one of the above

expl: Article 124 of the Constitution provides for the composition of the Supreme Court and states that it shall consist of a Chief Justice and 7 other judges, and that Parliament may, from time to time, determine the number of judges by law. To fix the number of judges, Parliament enacted the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956, and fixed the number of judges at 10 (excluding the Chief Justice). By amending this Act, the number of judges has been increased from time to time. Under the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019, the present maximum sanctioned strength of judges in the Supreme Court is 33 (excluding the Chief Justice).

stem: Who appoints the Judges of the Supreme Court of India?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / more than one of the above

expl: According to Article 124(2) of the Constitution of India, the President appoints every judge of the Supreme Court. The appointment of judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts is made on the recommendation of the Collegium system.

stem: A Judge of the Supreme Court may resign his office by writing to ?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: A judge of the Supreme Court may resign by writing to the President. In addition, on the recommendation of Parliament, the President can remove a judge from office. Notably, in Part V of the Constitution, Articles 124 to 147 deal with the establishment, independence, powers, procedure, and jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.

stem: What is the retirement age of the Judges of the Supreme Court ?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / more than one of the above

expl: According to Article 124(2) of the Constitution of India, the retirement age of Supreme Court judges is fixed at 65 years, whereas in the High Courts it is 62 years.

stem: The power to increase the number of Judges in the Supreme Court of India is vested in –
expl: Under Article 124 of the Constitution, Parliament has the power to increase the number of judges of the Supreme Court. It may be noted that the President has the power to determine the number of judges in the High Courts.

stem:
Consider the following statements about the collegium system :
1. The Supreme Court collegium is a five-member body, which is headed by the incumbent Chief Justice of India (CJI) and comprises four other seniormost Judges of the Court at that time.
2. The Parliament by law has evolved the collegium system.
3. The Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts are appointed only through the collegium system.
4. The collegium system was introduced in the year 1993 by Justice P. n. Bhagwati in the landmark First Judges Case.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
expl: The Supreme Court Collegium is a five-member headed by the current Chief Justice of India (CJI) and includes four other senior-most serving judges of the Court. Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts are appointed by the President on the recommendation of the Supreme Court Collegium. The Collegium system was not created by Parliament; rather, it evolved through Supreme Court judgments.

stem: Which of the following is concerned with the Supreme Court of India?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The Collegium system is the mechanism for the appointment of judges in the Supreme Court and High Courts, and for the transfer of High Court judges. It is a system developed through Supreme Court decisions. The Chief Justice of India leads the Collegium. Article 131 describes the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, while Articles 132 to 136 deal with its appellate jurisdiction. Hence, more than one option is correct.

stem: Judicial review means that the Supreme Court -

options.label: a
options.text: has final authority over all cases.

options.label: c
options.text: can review cases decided by the High Courts.

options.label: d
options.text: can declare any state law invalid

expl: Judicial review means that the Supreme Court and the High Courts can declare any law of any State/Centre invalid. If laws made by the Centre or any State violate constitutional provisions, the Supreme Court and the High Courts can declare them void. This power of the courts is called judicial review.

stem: Judicial process in India is based on -

options.label: b
options.text: The due process of routine law

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/more than one of the above

expl: In India, the judicial system is based on the Constitution, procedure established by law, and tradition.

stem: What position did A.S. Anand hold in the late 1990s?
expl: Justice Adarsh Sen Anand (A. S. Anand) was working as the 29th Chief Justice of India in the late 1990s. His tenure as Chief Justice was from 10 October, 1998 to 1 November, 2001.

stem: Which article of the Indian Constitution defines the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court?
expl: Article 131 defines the original jurisdiction (Original Jurisdiction) of the Supreme Court. According to this Article, in any dispute between the Government of India and one or more States, or between the Government of India and any State/States on one side and one or more other States on the other side, or between two or more States, if such a question of law or fact is involved on which the existence or extent of a legal right depends, then the Supreme Court will have original jurisdiction over it.

stem: The power of the Supreme Court of India to decide disputes between the Centre and the State falls under its :
expl: Article 131 defines the original jurisdiction (Original Jurisdiction) of the Supreme Court. According to this Article, in any dispute between the Government of India and one or more States, or between the Government of India and any State/States on one side and one or more other States on the other side, or between two or more States, if such a question of law or fact is involved on which the existence or extent of a legal right depends, then the Supreme Court will have original jurisdiction over it.

stem: The basis of judicial review in India is -

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More man one of me

expl: In India, the basis of judicial review is “procedure established by law”. Under this, the court examines whether a law has been made in accordance with the powers given to the legislature by the Constitution, and whether it follows the procedure established by law or not. If this procedure is violated, the law can be declared void by the court.

stem: Which of the following is related to the Supreme Court of India?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: In the Indian Constitution, provisions related to the Supreme Court are mentioned in Part 5, Chapter 4, in Articles 124 to 147. Note that the collegium system is the system for appointment and transfer of judges. It is a system developed through Supreme Court judgments. The Chief Justice of India leads the collegium. Under Article 131, the original jurisdiction/original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court is described, under which the Supreme Court decides disputes between the Centre and the States, and between two or more States. Further, Articles 132 to 136 mention the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court; therefore, more than one option is correct.
